description: Single-panel comparison plot of precipitation strengthening versus precipitate fraction, redrawn after ref. [140]. The y-axis is labelled "Precipitation strengthening (MPa)", linear 0-500 with major ticks every 100 (minor ticks at 25); the x-axis is labelled "Precipitaton fraction" (spelled as printed) and is logarithmic from 0.0001 to 1 with labelled ticks at 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1 and 1. Four outlined envelopes, each labelled inside, bound the reported ranges for individual carbides. The NbC envelope occupies the lowest fractions, roughly 0.0002-0.001, and strengthening up to between the 100 and 200 MPa gridlines. The VC envelope is the narrowest, a near-vertical strip around 0.001 at roughly 30-130 MPa. The TiC envelope spans about 0.002-0.004 and reaches the highest strengthening of the figure, peaking between the 400 and 500 MPa gridlines. The κ envelope sits at far larger fractions, roughly 0.06-0.35, at about 100-350 MPa. The figure's argument is that κ-carbides in Fe-Mn-Al-C steels strengthen at precipitate fractions one to two orders of magnitude higher than the NbC, VC and TiC carbides of microalloyed steels, with the κ field entirely separate from the other three.

subfigures.description: Log-linear envelope plot: y = 'Precipitation strengthening (MPa)' 0-500 linear, x = 'Precipitaton fraction' logarithmic 0.0001-1. Four labelled outline polygons: NbC (fraction ~0.0002-0.001, up to between the 100 and 200 MPa gridlines), VC (narrow strip near 0.001, roughly 30-130 MPa), TiC (~0.002-0.004, peaking between the 400 and 500 MPa gridlines), and κ (~0.06-0.35, about 100-350 MPa). No numeric data labels on the envelopes; values read only against gridlines.

observations.observation: The y-axis is labelled 'Precipitation strengthening (MPa)' and runs linearly from 0 to 500 in steps of 100, with minor ticks at 25 MPa intervals.
The x-axis is labelled 'Precipitaton fraction' (spelt this way, without the second 'i') and is logarithmic, with labelled ticks at 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1 and 1.
Four outline envelopes are drawn and labelled internally: NbC, VC, TiC and the Greek-letter label κ.
The NbC envelope covers the lowest precipitate fractions, approximately 0.0002 to 0.001, with strengthening rising from around the 50 MPa level to between the 100 and 200 MPa gridlines.
The VC envelope is the narrowest of the four, a near-vertical band near a fraction of 0.001 spanning roughly 30 to 130 MPa.
The TiC envelope extends from about 0.002 to 0.004 in fraction and reaches the highest strengthening plotted, peaking between the 400 and 500 MPa gridlines.
The κ envelope lies at by far the largest fractions, roughly 0.06 to 0.35, with strengthening between about 100 and 350 MPa.
The κ field does not overlap the NbC, VC or TiC fields on the x-axis: those microalloying carbides act at fractions near 10⁻³, whereas κ-carbide acts near 10⁻¹.
No numerical values are printed inside any envelope; the ranges can only be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption states the figure compares strengthening by κ-carbides in Fe-Mn-Al-C steels with other carbides used in microalloyed steels, citing reference [140].

The citing text states the strengthening potential of the κ'-phase is between 100 and 350 MPa for a volume fraction of approximately 0.05-0.35, which matches the position of the κ envelope drawn in the plot.
The caption renders the phase as 'j0-carbides' (an OCR corruption of κ-carbides), whereas the plot itself labels the phase with the single character 'κ'.

measured_quantities: precipitate fraction (volume fraction, dimensionless, plotted logarithmically)
